episode_title: Building Metrics That Matter: Leading vs. Lagging Indicators

sections.dialogue:
Lenny: Julie, how do you prevent product teams from obsessing over lagging metrics like Revenue or Monthly Active Users (MAU)?

Julie Zhuo: Revenue and MAU are lagging outcomes; by the time they drop, your product has been failing for months. High-performing teams focus obsessively on Leading Indicators—the specific, high-frequency user behaviors that directly predict long-term retention and customer satisfaction. At Facebook, we discovered that users who added 7 friends in their first 10 days retained at 3x the rate of others. That leading metric guided our entire onboarding experience. Find the earliest behavioral proxy for core value delivery.

Lenny: Why is every North Star Metric dangerous without a paired Counter-Metric?

Julie Zhuo: If you tell an engineering team to optimize push notification click-through rate (CTR), they can double it tomorrow by spamming users with clickbait notifications. But in doing so, they will destroy long-term trust and app uninstalls will skyrocket. Every North Star metric must have a paired Counter-Metric (Guardrail Metric). If your primary goal is notification engagement, your counter-metric must be push notification opt-out rate or app uninstalls. Guardrails ensure teams optimize for durable value rather than superficial local maxima.
